criteria.criterion: Run cargo test: a test drains two fake items where the first landing changes a crates/ file; it shows the rebuild step ran exactly once and the second item ran under the new build commit.
criteria.evidence: I ran `a_landing_that_changes_athenas_code_rebuilds_once_and_the_next_item_runs_under_the_new_build` and it passed. Item a lands `crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs` (the stub's `unrelated` path). The test asserts the first pass stops as Rebuilt with rebuilds == 1 and a ran under "old". It asserts the restart limits are 9 jobs and $8.20. Through follow_restart, it then asserts rebuilds is still 1 and that ran_under is [(a,old),(b,new)].

criteria.criterion: go, drain, audit and audience print the same one-line stale-build warning when the build commit is older than HEAD for the watched paths.
criteria.evidence: I read main.rs. `warn_if_stale(&athena)` runs right after `open(true)?` in the Audience, Audit, Go and Drain arms. It prints `Athena::stale_build()`, which uses the same `stale_build_line` that status uses (status.rs). That function runs `git diff --name-only <build> <head> -- BUILD_PATHS` after checking that the build commit is an ancestor of HEAD. Caveat: if athena.toml does not parse, open(true) fails first (see the findings).

criteria.criterion: The re-exec passes the remaining budget and job limit.
criteria.evidence: drain.rs `drain_with` computes jobs_left = max_jobs - started and budget_left = budget - spent and stores them in Report::restart. main.rs runs `drain::follow_restart(report, ..., |left| reexec(&drain::reexec_args(&left, json)))`. reexec_args gives `drain --budget <left> --rating-threshold <n> --job-limit <left> [--json]`, and these flags match the Drain command's arguments in main.rs. The test `the_new_binary_is_started_with_the_remaining_budget_and_job_limit` checks the argument list.

criteria.criterion: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy with -D warnings and cargo test all pass.
criteria.evidence: These are Athena's recorded checks on this tree: fmt passed, clippy -D warnings passed, and cargo test --locked passed with 1422 tests.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the self-rebuild and stale-build warning.
criteria.evidence: Two new bullets under Added: one for drain rebuilding and re-executing (the watched paths, the remaining budget and job limit, 'rebuild failed' with build output, a drain-stop winning over the restart) and one for the stale-build line in status, go, drain, audit and audience. Both match the code.

findings.summary: A file outside the expected deliverables is changed: crates/athena-cli/src/wiring.rs.
findings.evidence: `git diff HEAD~1 --stat` shows wiring.rs with 6 lines added (`installed_binary()`, which returns `$ATHENA_HOME/bin/athena`). It is small and supports the re-exec, but it is not on the expected deliverables list.

findings.summary: In the motivating case, a config the old binary cannot parse, go, drain, audit and audience fail before they print the stale-build line.
findings.evidence: wiring::open with writes=true returns the config error ('unknown field ...') before `warn_if_stale` is reached. Only `status` (writes=false) falls back to the builtin config and still shows the line. Within drain, the new rebuild makes this case unlikely. A manual `athena go` after such a landing would still fail without the warning.

findings.summary: A drain-stop issued just before the re-exec can be lost.
findings.evidence: drain_with checks steps.stop_requested() before deciding to restart. The re-exec'd `athena drain` then removes the stop file at startup ('A stop asked for before this run started belongs to an earlier run'), so a stop that arrives between that check and the new process starting is dropped. The window is small.

summary: The change does what the request asks. Drain now notices when a landing touches crates/, xtask/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock or setup.sh. Before the next job starts, it runs setup.sh once through an injectable `Steps::rebuild`. It then ends the pass as `rebuilt` and re-execs `$ATHENA_HOME/bin/athena drain` with the remaining budget, the remaining job limit and the same rating threshold. That install path matches what xtask's setup installs (I read `xtask/src/main.rs`). A failed rebuild stops the run as `rebuild failed` and prints the build output. `athena status` shows a stale-build line, also as `stale_build` in its JSON, and go, drain, audit and audience print the same line to stderr. I ran the 7 new tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs and all passed. They cover: one rebuild, with the second item running under the new build; a failed rebuild; the remaining limits passed to the new run; and the status line after a crates/ change but not after docs/ or records/ changes. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed. CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions.md (D140) describe the change correctly. I found three minor issues and no blockers: crates/athena-cli/src/wiring.rs is changed but is not on the deliverables list; when athena.toml has a field the old binary does not know (the 2026-10-26 case), go, drain, audit and audience fail at startup before the warning prints; and a drain-stop issued in the moment just before the re-exec is lost.
